verdicts.evidence: lines 144-152 Save calls renameTeam; 158-171 Submit calls inviteMember and re-renders; 173-184 Remove calls removeMember and re-renders; 197 Refresh calls load. Every button has a handler that does what its label names.

line 128: new Date(m.lastActive) with null lastActive renders an invented 1970 date for Sam Lee. Line 48: hardcoded 'No members' is shown before any data has arrived and stays after a failed load. Line 6 hardcodes the team name in the title.
Single-screen settings page; no step depends on answers given on an earlier step or screen. The vague confirm text is judged under FB-007.
Each task is one or two short inputs (line 40 team name; lines 56-58 email and role); no multi-step flow, no long free text.

lines 145 and 176 use native confirm('Are you sure?'), whose default button is OK, so Enter carries out the removal or rename. Line 58 preselects 'member', which is the safe role, but the dialog default is the unsafe action.
Settings screen with six occasional tasks of equal standing (lines 37-67); no single dominant frequent task.
lines 27-30 hero banner, lines 32-35 intro paragraph and three note boxes, line 66 Refresh button: none match a task in the brief.
Each card holds at most one primary button: line 41 Save, line 59 Submit, line 66 Refresh. Row Remove buttons (line 129) use the plain style.
Remove button itself is plain and in its own column (line 129), but line 176 confirms with native confirm() where OK is the default and Enter triggers the removal.
line 59 Submit starts disabled; line 155 keeps it disabled until the email matches a regex; no text near it says why. CSS line 16 only greys it out.
No title attributes, tooltips or hover cards anywhere in the markup or script.
line 33: 'Note: this page was built with vanilla JavaScript and talks to a simulated API.'
lines 33-35: three Note/Tip/Disclaimer boxes at the top of the page, none tied to a decision or placed at a control.
line 32: 'This page lets you manage your team. Use the first card to rename the team, the table below it to...' narrates the layout.
lines 38-39: heading 'Team name' directly followed by label 'Team name'. Lines 28-29: hero subtitle restates the heading; line 32 restates the section headings.
line 28 'Welcome back! Let's supercharge your team'; line 29 'beautifully organised'; lines 148 and 167 'successfully!' toasts with exclamation marks.
line 59 button labelled 'Submit'; line 41 'Save' and line 66 'Refresh' name no object; confirms at lines 145 and 176 offer native OK/Cancel.

line 132 prints raw keys as labels: weekly_digest, new_member, billing, mentions. Lines 125-127 and 58 show lower-case enum values as roles. Lines 150, 169, 182 show raw server messages such as 'VALIDATION: email_format'.

line 150 alert(e.message), line 169 alert('Error: ' + e.message), line 182 toast('Failed: ' + e.message) show 'ECONNRESET: socket hang up...', 'CONFLICT: member_exists', 'LIMIT: seats_exhausted' with no next step.
line 169 'Error: ...', line 182 'Failed: ...', line 189 'Failed to change role'; raw messages carry all-capitals codes.
With zero members render() (lines 121-130) sets the tbody to an empty string: headers and nothing below. The only empty text is the pre-load 'No members' at line 48, with no action.

Failed load (lines 139-141) only logs, leaving 'No members' from line 48, which reads as an empty team. A truly empty team shows a blank table body. No distinct messages or actions for the two causes.

lines 139-141: load failure only console.error, nothing on screen. Line 193: notification save failure only console.error. Line 161 resets the invite form before the call, so a failed invite loses the email. No retry offered on any failure.
Calls take 0.4 to 1.5 s (line 74). load (135-142), rename (144-152), invite (158-171), remove (173-184), role and notification changes (186-195) show no busy or loading indicator at all.
line 48: the tbody ships with 'No members' and load() (lines 135-142) shows no loading state, so the empty text is visible during the whole initial request.

line 128 has no handling for a missing lastActive; null becomes a 1970 date. Lines 19-20, 46-49: five-column table with no wrapping, truncation or overflow rules for the 57-character email. Line 123 injects names unescaped.

Team name is saved by an explicit Save (line 41). No beforeunload handler; line 120 render() overwrites a typed name whenever Refresh, an invite or a removal completes; a typed invite email is likewise dropped on reload. No prompt, no restore.

lines 55-56: email field has only the label 'Email', no format hint, while line 155 enforces a regex. First reading fails the strict test; second reading finds the label itself implies the format. Verdicts differed.
No optional fields: team name (line 40) and invite email (line 56) are both needed, and role (line 58) always has a value.
line 154-156: the input listener only toggles the Submit button's disabled state; no error text is ever shown while typing. Errors appear only after submit (lines 150, 169).
lines 150 and 169: rejected rename and invite are reported through alert(), not beside the field; no field is marked.
line 161: $('invite-form').reset() runs before the request, so when inviteMember rejects (line 168-170) the email and role are already gone.
No aria-invalid or aria-describedby anywhere; errors are alert() (lines 150, 169) and focus is not moved to the email or team name field after a rejection.
line 59 Submit has the disabled attribute from the start; line 155 enables it only when the email passes a regex; nothing explains what is missing.

lines 144-152: Save is never disabled or marked busy during renameTeam, so a second click sends a second request. Invite is inert only as a side effect of the reset at lines 161-162, with no busy state.

line 197 Refresh: nothing changes on screen until the call returns, and nothing at all if it fails. After the confirm, Save (146-148) and Remove (177-180) show no pressed or busy state for up to 1.5 s.
line 193: a failed notification save is only logged, the checkbox stays as clicked. Lines 139-141: a failed load or Refresh is only logged. Failures are not always stated.
lines 165-167: the new member row is rendered into the table and a toast 'Invite sent successfully!' is shown as well.
line 116: every toast is removed after 2000 ms, including the errors at line 182 ('Failed: ...') and line 189 ('Failed to change role').
line 145: renaming the team, which is fully reversible, is gated by confirm('Are you sure?') and offers no undo.
line 176: removing a member asks only 'Are you sure?' with native OK/Cancel; it does not name the person or say they lose access at once, and OK is the default.
line 145: a confirmation dialog guards Save on the team name, a routine save.

lines 187-189: a role select keeps the new value when changeRole fails (toast only, no revert). Lines 191-193: a checkbox keeps its new state when setNotification fails, with no message. Line 161 clears the invite form before the server answers.
The only modals are native confirm() (lines 145, 176) and alert() (lines 150, 169): each a single short decision or message, opened in response to a user action.
All dialogs are native browser confirm()/alert() (lines 145, 150, 169, 176), which take focus, hold it, close on Escape and return focus to the page.
lines 27-35: a gradient hero with a 32px heading (CSS lines 10-11), an intro paragraph and three note boxes come before the first working card and carry the most visual weight.
lines 27-30: hero section 'Welcome back! Let's supercharge your team' with subtitle sits above the working content.
No summary numbers, stat cards or charts on the page.
No filter, search or sort controls; the members table (lines 46-49) always shows the full list.
All controls are native and focusable: input (40, 56), select (58, 124), button (41, 59, 66, 129), checkbox (132); dialogs are native confirm/alert. No click-only custom widgets.
Colour carries no status, error, required or selection meaning; roles are text in selects and errors are text in alerts and toasts.

lines 112-117: toast() appends a plain div to the body with no role or aria-live; no live region exists in the page markup. Table and notification re-renders (lines 121, 131) are not announced either.
No accordions, disclosure buttons, custom menus or tabs; the only expanding controls are native select elements.

CSS lines 8-22 have no media queries and no overflow wrapper; the five-column table (lines 46-49) with a 57-character email, a select and a button per row cannot fit 375px, so the Remove column is pushed off the viewport.
